rule: Each claim names exactly one executable test under tests/. The tracker stores no status and no missing observation: a claim's status in an environment is 'pass', 'fail' or 'not run', derived from that environment's newest committed run record by re-running the test's pure check(record). A claim whose test does not exist, does not import, or does not define run/check/fixture/CLAIM_ID is refused.

claims.title: Truthful settlement
claims.claim: If the settlement endpoint reports finalizedSuccess and settlementConfirmed for a deploy, that deploy's effect is present at the finalised head on every validator and remains present through two further epoch boundaries.
claims.pass_condition: For one deploy id: the settlement response is finalizedSuccess with settlementConfirmed true; every validator reports the same finalised (height, hash); a marker written by the deploy reads back at that finalised block and at every later finalised head sampled; the deploy id never appears in a later block's rejectedDeploys.
claims.fail_condition: A confirmed settlement whose effect is absent at the finalised head on any validator; validators disagree on the finalised hash; or the deploy id appears in a later rejectedDeploys.
claims.observable: The settlement response, each validator's finalised (height, hash), the marker read at that block, and the per-block rejectedDeploys.
claims.negative_control: A marker absent before the write; a fixture where the effect is absent at the finalised head; a fixture where the deploy is final-scope rejected.

environment.local: local-4 (tools/devnet.sh; 2 GiB per validator, below the documented tier)
environment.public: testnet-4: four independent hosts on the selected release

claims.does_not_claim: A local pass is a mechanism check; the public claim needs testnet-4.

claims.title: Safety
claims.claim: No two conflicting finalised histories: every finalised block held by one validator is finalised by every validator at or above its height, and no finalised (height, hash) regresses across restart, replay or partition.
claims.pass_condition: For every sampled finalised block, every validator at or above its height reports it finalised; no finalised (height, hash) regresses; no two conflicting finalised histories are observed; the isolated victim keeps producing while its finalised fence stays frozen.
claims.fail_condition: A finalised block not finalised by another validator at or above its height; a finalised regression; or two conflicting finalised histories.
claims.observable: Per-validator finalised heads at each sample, the cross-node containment answers, and the finalised history over the window.
claims.negative_control: A producing split (the victim proposes while isolated); an equivocation injection under the allowed Byzantine bound.

environment.public: testnet-4 with a real partition and the operator window

claims.does_not_claim: The claim assumes the <=1/3 Byzantine/equivocation bound; without it an equivocator can back two quorums.

claims.title: State agreement across a merge
claims.claim: For the same accepted block on the same binary, every validator derives the same preStateHash and postStateHash and the same kept/rejected ledger; kept tuple-space effects are present and rejected effects absent.
claims.pass_condition: Across a defined window, every validator reports the same preStateHash, postStateHash and rejectedDeploys for every accepted block, and a kept marker is readable at the same block on every validator.
claims.fail_condition: Any preStateHash, postStateHash or rejectedDeploys disagreement for the same block; a same-block marker present on one validator and absent on another.
claims.observable: The per-block preStateHash, postStateHash and rejectedDeploys from every validator, plus a same-block marker read.
claims.negative_control: A fixture where the ledger differs; a native-write case (native absolute writes are excluded from FinalizedMerge.lean's unqualified law).
claims.does_not_claim: The claim is conditional on the same binary and conflict scope; block-merge.md records that two binaries can reject different chains at a merge.

claims.title: Recovery without loss
claims.claim: After one validator is stopped and restarted, or a partition heals, the survivors keep finalising; every deploy accepted by a survivor is resolved and its effect is in the post-recovery finalised state; the victim rejoins the same finalised head; no spurious self-replay or own-key halt fires.
claims.pass_condition: With one validator stopped, the survivors finalise past the kill; every deploy submitted to a survivor resolves and its effect is present at the post-recovery finalised head; after restart the victim reports the same finalised (height, hash) at least three heights above the baseline; no finalised height regresses and no fixed height changes hash; no own-key halt or self-replay is observed.
claims.fail_condition: Finality stalls; accepted work is lost; the rejoiner needs manual surgery; a finalised height regresses; or a spurious halt fires.
claims.observable: The survivors' finalised heads, every accepted deploy's resolution and effect at the post-recovery finalised head, the victim's boot ID and finalised head, and the own-key/self-replay counters.
claims.negative_control: The wrong-genesis and interrupted-restart arms; a deploy accepted only by the killed validator is not recoverable by design and must be declared, not counted.

environment.public: testnet-4 with a real host stop

claims.does_not_claim: A store loss needs a fresh data dir and a checkpoint join; 'no operator action' covers a verified restart, not a lost store.

claims.title: Overload refusal
claims.claim: At the configured admission/pool bound, the node refuses new work with HTTP 429 and Retry-After: 1, or gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (ingress-rate and pool-bound classes stated separately), returns no 5xx, stays alive, and loses no deploy it accepted.
claims.pass_condition: With the bound configured: every permit is held, further probes are refused with the named class and retry signal, no 5xx is returned, the unset/default control admits, the handler is reachable after release, and every accepted deploy id is still readable or explicitly failed.
claims.fail_condition: A 5xx under pressure; an accepted deploy that later disappears; an unbounded queue; an unset default that refuses; or a refusal class outside the vocabulary.
claims.observable: Accepted/refused counts, refusal class and retry signal, handler reachability after release, and the status of every accepted deploy id.
claims.negative_control: The unset-default arm must admit; the four named queue bounds; a refusal class outside the vocabulary.

environment.local: local-4 (one node, direct listener and in-process gRPC)

claims.does_not_claim: The opt-in in-flight cap is not the shipping default; the pool's count/byte/term/share/rate bounds are the intended throttle. Transport correctness across HTTP, direct HTTP, gRPC and a proxy is out of scope.

claims.title: Join and audit
claims.claim: A fresh node joining from a bootstrap receives the certified anchor, applies and hydrates it, and reaches the same finalised head and state; rnode audit reproduces the checkpoint claim from genesis.
claims.pass_condition: The joiner's served, received, restored and walked hashes agree for the certified anchor (equality with the served root is required only for a genesis anchor); a legacy certificate with no commitments is refused; rnode audit returns AGREE, its audited digest equals the accepted digest when the anchor is a checkpoint, and its derived root equals the checkpoint claim.
claims.fail_condition: The joiner receives but never applies; the restored state differs from the certified anchor; a certificate with no commitments is accepted; audit returns DISAGREE, a different digest, or a derivation over a different checkpoint.
claims.observable: The six-stage join chain, the certified anchor's post-state root and fringeState, the audited digest, and the audit verdict.
claims.negative_control: A send-log-only chain; a served/restored hash mismatch; a legacy certificate with no commitments.
claims.does_not_claim: A routable address is setup, not the claim; off-host transport and the loopback refusal are out of scope. Alternative-peer failover (M3-11) is separate and never landed.

claims.title: Upgrade compatibility
claims.claim: A mixed-version fleet either keeps one finalised chain and one state for a block produced during the window, or refuses on the consensus path; a populated store migrates; a binary refuses a store written by a newer format.
claims.pass_condition: During a mixed-version window, a block is produced and finalised with both binaries deriving the same postStateHash and rejectedDeploys, or the old node refuses on the consensus path; a populated-store copy/rollback/restart drill passes; a build refuses a store whose format marker is higher than the one it writes; after the swap the upgraded node reaches the same finalised head.
claims.fail_condition: Two versions finalise different blocks or derive different post-state hashes without a refusal; the old binary runs on a newer store; or the populated-store drill fails.
claims.observable: The mixed-version block's hashes and rejection ledger on both binaries, the store-format refusal, the populated-store drill verdict, and the post-swap finalised head.
claims.negative_control: A fresh-genesis run must not substitute for the populated-store arm; a legacy/no-commitment certificate must be refused.
